blocks.heading: What has to go right for RELX, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: Net asset value is the first driver. The base starts at £1,696m in October 2027 and rises through the forecast. The bear row contracts toward £82m, while the bull row reaches £3,608m. The starting point reflects reported equity of £1,238m at June 2026 after heavy capital returns. In 2025, shareholder payments were £2,681m against free cash flow of £2,271m. The base therefore assumes earnings rebuild equity while buybacks moderate after the £2,250m 2026 programme. The bear keeps payouts high; the bull assumes stronger earnings and lower future buybacks.

blocks.heading: How much cash does RELX really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow starts with cash from operations and subtracts capital spending and lease payments. In 2025, that produced £2,271m before share-based pay, above net income. The comparison is reassuring because cash did not depend mainly on unpaid customer invoices.

After £63m of share-based pay, real free cash flow was lower. That deduction recognises the ownership cost of employee shares. The central question is whether today’s software and content investment maintains existing products or funds additional growth.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for RELX today?

paragraphs.text: Cash flow and financing add the next layer. Enterprise value broadly combines the value of the shares with debt and cash, while net debt means borrowings minus cash. At 30 June 2026, RELX reported £8,733m of net debt and leverage of 2.3x.

dividend.title: RELX dividend: payment, cash cover and yield
dividend.meta_description: RELX paid 67.5p per share in 2025, while dividends and buybacks together exceeded free cash flow.
dividend.opening: RELX paid 67.5p per share in 2025, up from 49.8p in 2021, and its base forecast starts at 72.2p in October 2027. In 2025, free cash flow did not cover dividends and buybacks together; new borrowing helped fund distributions.
dividend.closing: The full RELX memo also covers RELX’s business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: How much does RELX pay in dividends over time?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise from a base of 72.2p in October 2027 to 82.6p. The bear path reaches only 71.7p, while the bull reaches 87.4p. The base follows the record of annual increases from 49.8p in 2021 to 67.5p in 2025. RELX targets dividends broadly in line with adjusted EPS and a payout of about half of earnings. The bear allows only restrained growth because first-half buybacks exceeded free cash flow; the bull requires stronger earnings and cash generation.

blocks.heading: Is RELX’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The 2025 shortfall came from the scale of shareholder payments. Dividends and buybacks together exceeded free cash flow, and payments to minority owners widened the gap. Asset sales were too small to close it. New borrowing therefore did more than replace maturing loans: it also helped fund distributions and other uses of cash.

blocks.heading: What is RELX’s dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: Its 4.7% free-cash-flow yield sits beside a 2.4% dividend yield and 3.1% buyback yield. Over five years, revenue growth was uneven, while operating margin and diluted EPS rose. Free cash flow computed from the company’s cash-flow statement—cash from operations minus capital spending—did not cover shareholder payments in 2025; buybacks exceeded first-half free cash flow in 2026. A 2025 share-count reduction helped EPS outpace underlying growth.
